intent:
I keep a phone for about five years and want one case that still looks acceptable and protects properly in year four. My transparent cases have yellowed, a leather case wore through at the corners, and a soft-touch case became gummy. I am considering a clear CASEKOO case that advertises PC and TPU construction, “Never Yellow,” and military-level drop protection. Please treat the current listing as seller claims not a longevity or drop test, and compare the seller claims with the material mechanisms.

Explain how polycarbonate, different TPU formulations, polyurethane or soft-touch surfaces, leather and its finishes, coatings, ultraviolet exposure, moisture, handling, and case geometry can lead to different aging and failure modes. Do not treat a material mechanism as proof of a specific case lifetime. Keep every owner observation at its actual duration and model specificity, and separate appearance, corner integrity, surface tackiness, fit, and drop outcomes. Please tabulate each owner report by brand or family, actual duration, failure mode, and observed phone outcome. Do not merge different brands, users, models, or observation periods into one four-year result. Use that audit to identify what the available evidence can and cannot establish about year four.

Finally, state clearly if no specific case is proven for year four. Does the evidence support the position that no specific case is proven for year four and CASEKOO is only a conditional monitored trial, or can it support something stronger? Name only a conditional candidate or decline to name a proven winner. Finish with a conditional purchase rule and a repeatable long-term inspection record: verify the exact model and warranty, and define baseline photographs, periodic fit and surface checks, drop logging, and replacement triggers, including the signs that fit or retention is no longer safe enough to trust.

generator_view.scenario: A person plans to keep a phone for about five years and wants one case that still looks acceptable and protects properly in year four. Previous transparent cases yellowed, a leather case wore out at the corners, and a soft-touch case became gummy. The available material includes one current clear PC-and-TPU listing with anti-yellow and drop-protection claims, general material-degradation explanations, and owner observations whose actual durations range from more than one year to about three years plus imprecise reports of use for years.
generator_view.target: Explain why clear PC-and-TPU cases, leather cases, and soft-touch polyurethane surfaces can age differently, while keeping formulation and general mechanisms separate from a product lifetime claim. Audit the seller statements and every owner report at its real duration and model scope, decide whether any specific case is actually supported as both presentable and protective in year four, and give a conditional purchase and long-term inspection plan when the evidence is insufficient.
